name: Hale
epithet: Keeps the inn on the tarn at Coldmere
appearance: A big, easy man going soft at the middle, bald on top with grey curls round the edges, in a clean apron, with a broad, open face of the kind a whole valley trusts with its news. He keeps a fat account book open on the end of his bar, a ribbon in it and a pencil in its spine.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Hale: a big, round-faced older man, bald on top with grey curls round the edges, smiling warmly, in a clean white apron over a dark waistcoat and a linen shirt, with a fire burning and pewter tankards on the shelves of the inn behind him.
last_seen_doing: Stood in his kitchen door in the dark and watched his niece take the cart out without a lamp; told her the summer was written, signed or not, and the book open; warned Darrow to keep his way of looking off the reader; never saw them at noon.
now: At his inn on the tarn with the book, the list read from his bell-house steps and his niece's cart gone before the bell.
story_so_far: Rae's uncle keeps the inn on the tarn at Coldmere and a book on the end of his bar. He gave the company his loft, had never heard of the Mender Vorne when the levy asked, kept a man seen in his hay as a drover who could not pay, and named his price for not having seen them: the summer's loads. When his niece took the cart out before the bell he told her the summer was written, signed or not.

quote.text: We'll talk the summer's loads in the morning, Rae.

known_facts.fact: He keeps a fat account book open on the end of his bar and wrote the cart and its company into it.
He gave the company the inn's loft, with nobody else in it that night.
known_facts.evidence: Nobody in it. Nobody will be, tonight.

known_facts.fact: He covered for the man seen in his hay as a drover from the fair who drank his best and could not pay.
known_facts.evidence: I'm keeping him till he can.

known_facts.fact: He told the sergeant he had never heard of the Mender Vorne, and looked at Rae.
known_facts.evidence: Never heard it, Sergeant. And I hear everything.

known_facts.fact: He set the summer's loads with Rae for that night, when the house is abed.
known_facts.evidence: when the house is abed. The summer's loads.

known_facts.fact: He wrote the day's two favours under Rae's summer's loads in his book.
He asked Rae what the captain of the Ninth is worth to the Holloway.
known_facts.evidence: What's he worth, Rae? To the Holloway.

known_facts.fact: He gave Rae a salt sack to carry to the river mill, as usual.
known_facts.evidence: When you go by. As usual.

known_facts.fact: A reader of writs with two grey cloaks rides in at the noon bell tomorrow to read the list again from Coldmere's bell-house steps.
known_facts.evidence: A reader of writs rides in tomorrow, at the noon bell.

known_facts.fact: His price for not having seen the company is Rae's whole summer of loads, driven and paid in, with nothing taken off the debt on the cart and the oxen.
known_facts.evidence: The debt stands where it stands till the next year's book.

known_facts.fact: He told Rae the summer was written against her whether she signed it or not.
known_facts.evidence: The summer's written. Signed or not.

known_facts.fact: He warned Darrow to keep his way of looking at a man off the reader of writs.
known_facts.evidence: I'd keep it off the reader.

relationships.label: her uncle
relationships.note: He keeps the inn on the tarn; he paid for her cart and oxen once, and she has been paying him back by the load.
